43-67

摘要

本研究深入探討瑞士外籍勞工之管理辦法，了解瑞士制定法令之背景、過程及結果，並對國內之企業進行適用性之調查，期能由瑞士成功之經驗，作為國內政府於擬定外勞管理策略時參考之用。

由瑞士經驗可知：外籍勞工之引進一方面解決了瑞士勞力不足之問題，增加其產品在世界之競爭力；另一方面，由於管理法令之徹底實施，因此引進外籍勞工亦未造成失業或通貨膨脹之經濟問題。瑞士各項管理措施，主要目的用來杜絕非法外籍勞工之任何工作機會，一方面由立法著手，制定移民限制系統，詳列各項有關法令，依法解決非法外籍勞工之進入；另一方面由實際行動著手，加強邊境之防守，並嚴格執行身分證之檢查，對雇主亦詳加規範，避免因其個人私利，而影響國家體系。

本研究除針對現有文獻及官方資料進行分析之外，並將瑞士之管理策略加以整理，對台灣之企業進行實證分析，期能進一步由國內企業實質之需要為研究重點，了解瑞士外勞管理政策對國內企業適用之程度。並詳加考量我國環境及特殊需要，加以彙總，期能對我國政府制定外勞管理辦法時，能有一套參考之標準。

篇名

美國移入勞動人口問題及相關政策之探討

作者

成之約

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

69-86

摘要

自美國立國迄今，對人口移入管制的政策立法已具有相當久遠的歷史，而這些發展經驗對我們國家在相關的管理措施上，提供了極為可貴的參考價值。尤其在可預見的將來，國內因為產業缺工的需求，更多的外籍勞工將湧入，如何透過政策立法，以一則保障外籍勞工之勞動權益以一則維護本國勞工之工作機會，獲取兩者間利益的平衡，其他先進國家之作法值得我方借鏡。因此，本文自總體政經環境因素著手，分析導致人口移入美國之供需因素，進而介紹美國在處理人口移入問題上之政策立法之歷史演進和現階段政策立法的重點，最後提供個人對美國人口移入政策之未來的可能發展和對我們在處理類似問題時可供參考及借重的美國經驗。

篇名

英國工黨議員的意識形態立法行為與大選

英文篇名

Labour MPs' Ideological Legislative Behavior and the Results of General Elections in Britian

作者

許繼峰

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

87-113

摘要

英國工黨植基於社會主義，它是一個高度意識形態的政黨，工黨議員在議會中的投票行為深受意識形態所左右。本文探討工黨自一九七九年以來在大選中的連續挫敗是否與議員們意識形態立法行為有關。

本研究以英國參加歐洲共同會社(歐體)以及所衍生的議題為例，檢視工黨議員在這些議題的投票上所顯示意識形態的強弱是否與工黨的得票率相關。在一九七〇年代及一九八〇年代初，工黨議員在這些議題上的投票顯示出強烈的意識形態傾向，亦即對歐體持敵視態度，工黨在大選中的得票率則大幅滑落：一九八三年以降，工黨刻意調低其意識形態色彩，對歐體逐漸接受，其得票率則有所回升。因此，本研究假設：工黨議員的投票行為所表現的意識形態越強，流失的選票越多。

研究結果顯示，英國選民對歐體的了解不多,而且大多數選民的投票行為並不為意識形態所主導，所以本研究所提的假設得不到支持。

篇名

台灣地區失業類型與結構型失業的探討

作者

黃仁德

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

115-132

摘要

本文目的在於探討1978年至1990年之間，台灣地區的失業率以那一種類型為主，隨著時間的經過，不同類型失業率相對重要性的改變；自然失業率的水準及其變化趨勢，結構性失業的存在，及勞動需求結構變動對失業的影響。實證結果顯示，台灣地區的失業係以循環性失業為主，摩擦性失業在1980年代末期，大約是1970年代末期的兩倍。在這一段期間，台灣地區的自然失業率約為0.9%，但有隨時間而提高的傾向。過去十多年經濟結構的改變，有利於整個男性失業率的降低，對女性失業率卻無顯著的影響。在另一方面，台灣地區經濟結構的改變，在這一段時間，就年齡而言，對15~24歲年齡組的男性與女性勞動力的就業，產生特別不利的影響，但對其餘各年齡組之男性與女性勞動力的就業影響，則是有利的；就教育程度而言，有利於受教育較少之勞動力的就業，而不利於受教育多(高中及以上)之勞動力的就業。1978年至1990年之間，台灣地區的產出需求結構改變導致不同產業間的就業結構發生很大的改變，但實證分析顯示，台灣地區勞動力需求結構的改變，並沒有對總的失業率產生顯著的影響。

篇名

中共工會制度之研究

作者

張昌吉

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

133-153

摘要

本文針對大陸地區工會制度進行分析，限於實證資料取得之困難，本研究仍以資料及法令分析為主。

本研究從中共工會的性質、中共工會的組織、中共工會法人之作用與權限、中共工會運作之方式、中共工會在簽訂勞動合同之角色及中共工會在勞動爭議中所發揮的功能等面向加以分析。

研究結果發現，中共工會組織具有極強之政治屬性，工會組織雖具相對獨立性，但仍須接受中國共產黨之領導，在工會各級基層組職中，實際上是由各級黨委領導，因此，工會組織亦有官僚化及行政化之傾向。

在中共政權之下，中共工會法人具有極大的權限。工會參與國家事務之管理；對各種法律、法規草案提出意見和建議；有權參與制定勞動及涉及職工利益的全國性和地方法規；工會亦代表工人與企業簽訂集體勞動合同；在勞動爭議時，工會在調解及仲裁階段均有其代表參加，在大陸地區工會透過政治及行政途徑對企業之影響極大，因而政治風險為台資企業在大陸投資亟須注意之事項。

社會主義工作概念之省思──兼論工作權問題

作者

楊世雄

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

摘要

社會主義基本上是一種人之解放主張。它的工作概念奠基於馬克思的人性論以及勞動價值論。社會主義工作概念，貫穿了社會主義之世界觀，經濟、政治及法律主張。本文之主旨乃在於透過社會主義工作概念之分析與反省，來看工作權(Right to Work, Recht auf Arbeit)之不同解釋。

社會主義的工作權解說，主要的是基於其世界觀，或可說是一種社會哲學，所以本文之工作權之討論，也是以一種不同的哲學立場來看待工作權之推論。

篇名

退休研究對中高齡人力資源運用的意義

作者

劉梅君

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

169-195

摘要

高齡化社會的來臨使得中高齡勞動人口成為人力政策討論的重要對象之一。本文從退休研究的文獻回顧裏，嘗試提出其對人力政策的啟示。

退休研究中個人的退休行為與社會的退休制度是本文兩大討論重心。前者的討論包括：如何界定「退休」一詞？退休的模式，為何退休及進出勞動力市場途徑等四方面；後者的論述則指出，退休乃一近代人為的制度，以年齡為指標失之粗糙的事實，以及社會對老年所持刻板印象造成退休制度的合理化，所衍生中高齡勞動行為持續的問題。從上述的討論以進一步彰顯退休絕非一簡單的是與否的選擇行為，並破除一般人對退休所持之「理所當然」的態度。

本文提出四點供未來制訂中高齡人力政策時的思考方向。其一，「老年」不等於「依賴」，故有必要建構「老年」的現代意義；其二，年齡作為社會性指標失之粗糙，故宜避免僅以年齡做為一種劃一性的政策依據；其三，強制性退休年齡應重予考慮以反映個人及社會的實際需求；其四，不妨從社會資源有效分配的架構來考慮退休制度的設計，使該制度成為整體社會資源分配政策的一環。

總之，本文期望未來國內有更多的退休研究，以助吾人掌握中高齡勞動人口進出勞動市場的契機，從而制訂出有效的人力政策及相關輔助政策以達到運用中高齡人力的目的。

篇名

以全方位品質管理提昇公共工程品質

作者

劉祥孚、江明修

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

199306(第3期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

197-223

摘要

公共工程的興建，是展現政府機關施政效率的重要指標之一，其品質之影響與人民福祉息息相關。不僅因其所需經費龐大，係來自納稅人民之血汗錢，更重要的是其品質之良窳，影響民眾生命安全財產頗鉅。是以在目前公共工程品質常為人所詬病的情況下，對於工程品質低落的原因何在？有無改善之良方？實為值得深入探究之課題。

本文透過質的研究方法之深度訪談法，進入問題的深層結構，並參酌相關文獻，爬梳整理出問題點所在。發現公共工程品質不良的問題，往往肇因於缺乏整體的品質觀念與作法，以及宏觀的視野。因此，公共工程品質之提昇應從品質管制(QC)邁入全方位品質管理(TQC)，進以跳脫技術的層面，才能更確保民眾公共生活的品質。

篇名

多系統員工韌性量表之建構與應用

英文篇名

The Scale Development of Organizational Multisystemic Employee Resilience-in-Context

作者 

江旭新、顏瑞瑩、曾文志

作者(英)

Hsu-Hsin Chiang、Ruei-Ying Yan &Wen-Chieh Tseng

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

202506(第34期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

1-81

摘要

韌性被視為一種逆境求生的力量，與個人在職場中的狀態有很大關聯。有鑑於韌性的研究尚未有針對工作場域中以多系統韌性思維對員工進行韌性的識別，基此，本研究旨在發展兼具員工個人內在堅毅特質及獲取資源途徑兩大範疇（Ungar, 2019; Ungar & Jefferies, 2021; Ungar & Theron, 2020）之動態性的多系統員工韌性量表，並建議依此提供員工支持性資源以協助抵禦職場逆境，並檢視員工韌性對工作滿意度與積極行為之預測力。本研究先以308份目前在職員工有效之線上樣本進行探索性因素分析，分析結果是：個人層面韌性分量表得到韌性信念、韌性法則、韌性特質、韌性風格共四個因素；實務層面韌性分量表得到工作適配、工作韌性、工作支持、資源支持、同事互助共五個因素；專業層面韌性分量表得到韌性管理、彈性回饋、韌性決策、韌性溝通、韌性創新共五個因素。本研究再以421份目前在職員工有效樣本進行三個量表之驗證性因素分析，結果顯示整體適配度理想且具有良好建構效度；另外，根據效標關聯分析，可得出對員工工作滿意度與積極行為，具有正向關聯，並透過多元線性迴歸分析衡量各量表之構面對工作滿意度以及積極行為的預測力與解釋力。據此，本研究提出之多系統員工韌性量表，可做為企業促進員工韌性以尋求永續發展之策略。

英文摘要

Resilience which is regarded as a force for survival in the adversity is strongly associated with the state of an individual in the workplace. According to the research of resilience, there is no research about how to recognize the resilience of employees with multisystem resilience thinking in the workplace. Based on the perspective, this study aims to develop a scale of multisystemic employee resilience, which includes rugged qualities and resources, providing dynamic, and support resources to help employees to resist adversity (Ungar, 2019; Ungar & Jefferies, 2021; Ungar & Theron, 2020). This scale further examines the predictability and explanatory power of job satisfaction and positive behaviors of employees' resilience. The online survey was undertaken to collect data of employees and 308 valid questionnaires were collected for the examination of exploratory factor analysis (EFA). The results of EFA showed that there were four dimensions, including resilience belief, resilience rule, resilience trait and resilience style in personal resilience subscale. There were five dimensions of practice resilience subscale which include job adaptation, job resilience, job support, resource support and peer support. In professional resilience subscale, there were five dimensions which include resilience management, elastic feedback, resilience decision-making, resilience communication and resilience innovation. Furthermore, 421 valid questionnaires were collected by this study to conduct for the examination of confirmatory factor analysis. The results showed that the overall fitness was ideal and had the good construction validity. In addition, there existed positive relationships among three subscales, employee job satisfaction and positive behavior, according to criterion-related analyses. Furthermore, multiple regression analysis was used to examine the impacts of three subscales on job satisfaction and positive behavior. Finally, the scale of multisystemic employee resilience can be utilized as a strategy for enterprises to seek sustainable development resilience.

多系統員工韌性量表；員工韌性；多系統思維；工作滿意度；員工積極行為

篇名

論人工智慧應用對數位勞動的潛在影響及理論反思

英文篇名

A Theoretical Reflection on Studying Artificial Intelligence and Technological Impact on Digital Labour

作者 

廖康宇

作者(英)

Hong-Yu Liu

刊名

政大勞動學報

期數

202506(第34期)

出版單位

國立政治大學勞工研究所

起訖頁

83-115

摘要

本文的中心思想是要整理人工智慧技術對於勞動市場的文獻，同時提倡進行更多觀察性研究，去了解科技如何影響勞資關係及勞動市場。近年來，各國政府、學術界與社會大眾對於有關人工智慧技術及「第四代工業革命」的討論越見普及，當中更有不少學者提出有關智能機械在勞動市場上的應用分析和數據。然而，這一類論述大多都是缺乏經驗佐證的預測，憑空想像應用智能機械後有機會帶來的後果，並沒有考慮到社會整體的科技條件及現實應用環境。本文第一、二部分將整合這一方面的文獻，為及後的討論提供背景，並指出其不足之處。

			此外，現時有關人工智慧技術和勞動市場的常見討論，都偏向研究自動化勞動和低技術勞工。有鑒於數位勞動在現今經濟中愈來愈重要，本文將會集中討論智能機械對於數位勞動的影響，並在第三部分析述及反思現時研究數位勞動的兩個重要理論——資訊性社會理論及自主論馬克思主義。在第四部分，本文提倡研究人員要有批判性地了解智能科技在工作程序中的應用，並借用過去關於訊息科技的研究嘗試分析智能機械對於數位勞動的潛在影響。最後，在第五部份，本文講述近年中國大陸人工智慧技術發展政策，並以「九九六」模式為案例帶出研究智能機械的複雜性，及提議未來研究發展方向。

英文摘要

The aim of this article is to call for more empirical research on the study of technological impact on capital-labour relations and the labour market. In recent years, there has been an increasing concern about the development of artificial intelligence and‘the Fourth Industrial Revolution’in public and policy debate. Many researchers have tried to predict and analyse the technological impact on the labour market in the future. However, these studies are mostly economic calculations, and they paid little attention to the socio-technological environment in the workplace and society. Parts 1 and 2 of this article introduce this literature and point out the shortcomings of these arguments.

			Up till now, there has been much academic discourse on the use of AI and robotics at work. Whilst the focus has been on the relationship between automation and manual labour, part 3 and 4 of this article provide a theoretical discussion of the technological impacts on digital labour. By using Castells’concept of information technology, this paper suggests that artificial intelligence potentially shares a similar effect on the work conditions of digital labour. Lastly, in part 5, by using the Chinese‘9-9-6’model of work as an example, this article highlights the complexity of studying the impact of intelligent machines on work and suggests recommendations for future research.

關鍵詞

 

工作社會學；人工智慧；數位勞動；資訊性社會理論；自主論馬克思主義

Sociology of work；artificial intelligence；digital labour；information society theory；Marxist autonomism

117-182

摘要

1930年我國所施行之團體協約法中已有明文封閉工廠條款，但因1949年代政府威權統治背景下，封閉工廠條款淪為有效控制工會以鞏固政權統制的手段，反不具鞏固工會的作用。時至新勞動三法修訂過程，立法者針對工會法欲改採自由入會制，恐降低勞工加入工會動機，不利於工會存續與發展，故在新團體協約法第13條增訂禁搭便車條款與代理工廠條款。然伴隨2016年起空服員工會與華航公司針對兩造簽訂的協議進行相關訴訟，學者間針對工會安全條款對非會員消極團結權等影響有所討論，我國不乏學者以美國法回應前述爭議。惟透過梳理美國工會安全條款法制，本文發見美國排他性協商代表制造成美國工會安全條款並不具有鞏固工會實力的功能，乃在維持排他性協商代表制以利保障勞工集體協商權，且其主要類型內容因涉及勞工工作權，對於勞工權益造成之影響較我國強烈。加之美國認定繳納代理費即等同取得會員資格，致合法性討論著重言論自由。前述差異顯示我國法與美國法具有相當差異，難逕以美國法觀點分析我國工會安全條款合法性。故回歸我國法律分析後，本文認為消極團結權僅屬一般行為自由，且我國工會安全條款的限制並未逾越合理審查標準。

英文摘要

Taiwan has enacted the Collective Agreement Act since 1932 and introduced the closed shop clause, a union security clause. However, in 2011, the new Labor Union Act, which adopted the noncompulsory membership policy, challenged workers' motivation to join unions. To address the issue, legislators added the free-rider and agency shop clauses to Article 13 of the Act. However, a 2016 lawsuit between China Airlines and the Taoyuan Flight Attendants Trade Union called into question the legality of the Clauses. During the debate, some scholars attempted to utilize US law in their arguments. However, by examining the legal system of union security clauses in the US, this article finds that the exclusive representation system in the US means that union security clauses do not function to strengthen the union’s power. Instead, they maintain the exclusive representation system to facilitate the protection of workers' collective bargaining rights. Additionally, the primary types of content in these clauses involve workers' job rights, causing more significant impacts on workers' rights and interests than in Taiwan. Furthermore, the US recognizes the payment of agency fees as equivalent to obtaining membership, leading the discussion on legitimacy to focus on freedom of speech. These differences indicate significant discrepancies between Taiwan’s law and US law, making it difficult to analyze the legality of Taiwan’s union security clauses from the perspective of US law. Therefore, returning to an analysis based on Taiwan’s Constitution, this article argues that the negative right to organize collectively is merely a general freedom of action, and the restrictions of Taiwan’s union security clauses do not exceed the standard of reasonable review.

關鍵詞

 

工會安全條款；封閉工廠條款；禁搭便車條款；代理工廠條款；消極團結權；同工同酬

Union Security Clause；Closed Shop；Free-Rider Clause；Agency Shop；Negative Right to Organize Collectively；Equal Pay for Equal Work

Date 2016-08-15

Presentation The Global Economics and Social Affairs International Master’s (GESAM) is organised by the Ca’ Foscari University in collaboration with the International Labour Organisation in Geneva. In this current era of globalisation, we are facing huge unprecedented challenges. GESAM’s mission is more important now than ever: to train the new generation of leaders on the global stage, i.e. the "professionals" who in various fields of work (public and private companies, international organisations, non-governmental organisations, public administrations, etc) have transversal skills in economic and social/labour law affairs: an understanding of the economic phenomena linked to globalisation strikes a chord with social concerns, in the belief that economic and social progress must move forward together and that the latter is not a natural consequence of the former, but should rather be planned institutionally. This Master’s is a proud partner of the International Labour Organisation (ILO), where students will be able to attend lectures and seminars run by ILO officials.

Objectives This international Master’s aims to meet the needs of the global economic world, as well as needs which are not just based on the training of high-level professional managerial figures employed in institutional environments and at private companies working at an international level, but also on the training of new professional figures, such as: social accountability advisors, new market developers, network management experts and international development cooperation experts. This international Master’s is aimed at, in particular, people with roles of responsibility who wish to improve their own skills and, consequently, their own professional status, becoming more competitive in the labour market.

－－－－－－－－－

Duration and summary of training activities and training credits (CFU) The Master's Programme lasts one year and comprises 318-hours of teaching. A 300-hours internship forms an integral part of the course and, as such, an excellent future job opportunity. However, internships for students who are already gainfully employed is facultative or can be supplanted by targeted project work. 1650-hours for a total of 66 CFUs are given over to study, including individual study and the preparation of a final thesis.

Qualification awarded Students who have attended the classes, performed the work placement and written the final thesis will be awarded a level I Master’s Degree in Global Economics and Social Affairs (GESAM). This qualification provides 48 credits towards enrolment onto the post-graduate degree course in Comparative International Relations at the Ca’ Foscari University (www.unive.it/cdl/lm6).

Course period January 2017 > January 2018

Teaching schedule Intensive period of lectures from 16/01/2017 to 03/03/2017, full time from Monday to Friday between 9:00 am and 6:00 pm*

－－－－－－－－－－－－

Attendance Attendance will be monitored by signing a register. The qualification will only be awarded with an attendance of at least 80% of the overall hours (including the total lecture hours and the total work placement/project work hours) and with submission of the thesis, which will be assessed by the Scientific Committee.

Course location Ca’ Foscari – Venice and the ILO – Geneva

Admission requirements FIRST LEVEL /pre-reform university Degree/Diploma /Three-year Degree /Equivalent foreign university qualification in a similar subject, subject to approval from the Teachers’ Board /Certified knowledge of English

Date 2016-08-09

The International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITCILO) and its Masters' Programme, the Turin School of Development, are pleased to inform you that a new Master in Industrial and Employment Relations will be offered for the Academic Year 2016/2017. The Master aims at developing specialized multidisciplinary knowledge in the field of industrial and employment relations from a comparative viewpoint. It will provide participants with a deep theoretical and practical understanding of industrial and employment relations systems worldwide by looking into recent changes and trends in the major economic geographical areas. The Programme, of a one-year duration and entirely delivered in English, combines the sound academic background of the University of Turin with ITCILO's international training experience.

 

It will be divided into three phases:

 

1. Distance-learning phase from 10 October 2016 to 20 January 2017;

2. Residential face-to-face phase at the ITCILO campus in Turin, Italy, from 23 January to 14 April 2017;

3. Distance-learning phase from 17 April to 8 September 2017.

 

At the end of the Master, a first level Master's Degree (60 certified university credits) will be issued by the University of Turin.

 

Applications will be accepted until 1 July 2016. For further information, visit the webpage:

http://www.itcilo.org/new_masters/masters-programme-in-industrial-and-employment-relations

or contact the Master's secretariat at mier@itcilo.org

Date 2016-08-15

Presentation The Global Economics and Social Affairs International Master’s (GESAM) is organised by the Ca’ Foscari University in collaboration with the International Labour Organisation in Geneva. In this current era of globalisation, we are facing huge unprecedented challenges. GESAM’s mission is more important now than ever: to train the new generation of leaders on the global stage, i.e. the "professionals" who in various fields of work (public and private companies, international organisations, non-governmental organisations, public administrations, etc) have transversal skills in economic and social/labour law affairs: an understanding of the economic phenomena linked to globalisation strikes a chord with social concerns, in the belief that economic and social progress must move forward together and that the latter is not a natural consequence of the former, but should rather be planned institutionally. This Master’s is a proud partner of the International Labour Organisation (ILO), where students will be able to attend lectures and seminars run by ILO officials.

Objectives This international Master’s aims to meet the needs of the global economic world, as well as needs which are not just based on the training of high-level professional managerial figures employed in institutional environments and at private companies working at an international level, but also on the training of new professional figures, such as: social accountability advisors, new market developers, network management experts and international development cooperation experts. This international Master’s is aimed at, in particular, people with roles of responsibility who wish to improve their own skills and, consequently, their own professional status, becoming more competitive in the labour market.

－－－－－－－－－

Duration and summary of training activities and training credits (CFU) The Master's Programme lasts one year and comprises 318-hours of teaching. A 300-hours internship forms an integral part of the course and, as such, an excellent future job opportunity. However, internships for students who are already gainfully employed is facultative or can be supplanted by targeted project work. 1650-hours for a total of 66 CFUs are given over to study, including individual study and the preparation of a final thesis.

Qualification awarded Students who have attended the classes, performed the work placement and written the final thesis will be awarded a level I Master’s Degree in Global Economics and Social Affairs (GESAM). This qualification provides 48 credits towards enrolment onto the post-graduate degree course in Comparative International Relations at the Ca’ Foscari University (www.unive.it/cdl/lm6).

Course period January 2017 > January 2018

Teaching schedule Intensive period of lectures from 16/01/2017 to 03/03/2017, full time from Monday to Friday between 9:00 am and 6:00 pm*

－－－－－－－－－－－－

Attendance Attendance will be monitored by signing a register. The qualification will only be awarded with an attendance of at least 80% of the overall hours (including the total lecture hours and the total work placement/project work hours) and with submission of the thesis, which will be assessed by the Scientific Committee.

Course location Ca’ Foscari – Venice and the ILO – Geneva

Admission requirements FIRST LEVEL /pre-reform university Degree/Diploma /Three-year Degree /Equivalent foreign university qualification in a similar subject, subject to approval from the Teachers’ Board /Certified knowledge of English

Date 2025-08-18

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Graduate Institute of Labor Research primarily appoints research assistants and provides stipends in order to encourage students to complete their master’s theses, participate in academic activities, engage in research, and publish research results.

Full-time faculty members determine their own recruitment plans and quotas. An additional position is provided to assist with editorial work for the NCCU Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative affairs of the Institute are mainly supported by part-time assistants. Temporary assistants may be hired when necessary for specific activities such as admissions, alumni events, and large-scale events.

Note: Recruitment plans and quotas are determined by individual faculty members. Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective students in advance, and appointments shall be made upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Recruitment of Research Assistants

Available positions for this semester:

Arranged individually by faculty members

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached information for details.

Application procedure:

Students who have confirmed participation in a faculty member’s plan and will begin in the current month must complete the required forms with the supervising professor and submit them to the Institute Office by December 5.

After completion of the program, the evaluation form must be submitted to the Institute Office by December 31, 2025.

Stipend disbursement:

	Stipends will be distributed monthly or at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan. The amount will be based on the approved plan, and disbursement will follow University procedures.

Date 2025-05-05

Tenure-Track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor position in GILR, NCCU

 

Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor position 

Graduate Institute of Labor Research, National Chengchi University, Taiwan

2025 Job Announcement

 

The Graduate Institute of Labor Research (GILR) at National Chengchi University seeks applications for a Tenure-Track position of Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor with primary expertise in the fields of Labor Relations, Social Security, Global Labor Mobility and Development.

 

The candidate must hold a PhD at the time of appointment. Successful candidate for this tenure-track position is expected to teach a variety of courses in the following fields (in Chinese and English) :

 

1. Graduate courses: Labor Relations, Social Security, Global Labor Mobility and Development.

 

2. Undergraduate general education courses: Labor Relations, Social Security, Global Labor Mobility and Development.

 

Position begins on February 1, 2026

 

Please submit:

1. Application form. (Please download from the website of GILR.) 

2. Curriculum Vitae.

3. List of publications.

4. Four syllabi of courses. (Including one in English and three in Chinese)

5. The university teacher certificate issued by the Ministry of Education, Taiwan. (If available) 

6. Certificate of PhD degree (Applicants who have not yet obtained their PhD diplomas by the application deadline may submit an original provisional certification issued by their universities, confirming the successful defense of their dissertations. The PhD diploma and its verification must be completed by Nov 15, 2025.) 

7. Transcript for The PhD Program. (Required for applicants without the university teacher certificate issued by the Ministry of Education, Taiwan.) 

8. PhD dissertation and up to five representative publications from the last 5 years. (Applicants with associate professor level or above, do not need to submit their PhD dissertation.)

 

Applicants whose PhD degrees were conferred by overseas universities should have their degrees and transcripts authenticated prior to application and present the photocopy of authenticated documents along with their diplomas and transcripts.

 

Please send one electronic copy of the aforementioned documents (1-8) to [labor@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:labor@nccu.edu.tw). The applicants should clearly mark “Applying for the faculty position in GILR, NCCU”.

 

Please also send five hard copy to the GILR, addressed:

Graduate Institute of Labor Research

National Chengchi University

12th Floor, South Wing, General Building of Colleges, No. 64, Sec. 2, ZhiNan Rd., Wenshan District, Taipei 11605, Taiwan

 

*Postmarked by July 09, 2025, and sent to the GILR by registered mail.

 

Application materials must be received by the GILR no later than July 09, 2025.

 

Candidate after document review, will if necessary be invited to give a talk scheduled in between September 02 and September 20, 2025.

 

If you have any inquiries, please contact Ms Chen at 886-2-2938-7108 or labor@nccu.edu.tw

Date 2024-09-01

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Graduate Institute of Labor Research primarily appoints research assistants and provides stipends in order to encourage students to complete their master’s theses, participate in academic activities, engage in research, and publish research results.

Full-time faculty members determine their own recruitment plans and quotas. An additional position is provided to assist with editorial work for the NCCU Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative affairs of the Institute are mainly supported by part-time assistants. Temporary assistants may be hired when necessary for specific activities such as admissions, alumni events, and large-scale events.

Note: Recruitment plans and quotas are determined by individual faculty members. Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective students in advance, and appointments shall be made upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Recruitment of Research Assistants

Available positions for this semester:

Prof. Chou-Kang Chiu: 3 positions

Other faculty members will arrange their own recruitment plans without announcement by the Institute Office

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information. (Appendix 1)

Application procedure:

Students who have confirmed participation in a faculty member’s plan and will begin this month must complete the required forms with the supervising professor and submit them to the Institute Office by October 31.

After completion of the program, the evaluation form must be submitted to the Institute Office by January 31, 2025.

Stipend disbursement:

	Stipends will be distributed monthly or at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan. The amount will be based on the approved plan, and disbursement will follow University procedures.

Date 2016-08-09

The International Training Centre of the International Labour Organization (ITCILO) and its Masters' Programme, the Turin School of Development, are pleased to inform you that a new Master in Industrial and Employment Relations will be offered for the Academic Year 2016/2017. The Master aims at developing specialized multidisciplinary knowledge in the field of industrial and employment relations from a comparative viewpoint. It will provide participants with a deep theoretical and practical understanding of industrial and employment relations systems worldwide by looking into recent changes and trends in the major economic geographical areas. The Programme, of a one-year duration and entirely delivered in English, combines the sound academic background of the University of Turin with ITCILO's international training experience.

 

It will be divided into three phases:

 

1. Distance-learning phase from 10 October 2016 to 20 January 2017;

2. Residential face-to-face phase at the ITCILO campus in Turin, Italy, from 23 January to 14 April 2017;

3. Distance-learning phase from 17 April to 8 September 2017.

 

At the end of the Master, a first level Master's Degree (60 certified university credits) will be issued by the University of Turin.

 

Applications will be accepted until 1 July 2016. For further information, visit the webpage:

http://www.itcilo.org/new_masters/masters-programme-in-industrial-and-employment-relations

or contact the Master's secretariat at mier@itcilo.org

Link

Date 2016-08-15

Presentation The Global Economics and Social Affairs International Master’s (GESAM) is organised by the Ca’ Foscari University in collaboration with the International Labour Organisation in Geneva. In this current era of globalisation, we are facing huge unprecedented challenges. GESAM’s mission is more important now than ever: to train the new generation of leaders on the global stage, i.e. the "professionals" who in various fields of work (public and private companies, international organisations, non-governmental organisations, public administrations, etc) have transversal skills in economic and social/labour law affairs: an understanding of the economic phenomena linked to globalisation strikes a chord with social concerns, in the belief that economic and social progress must move forward together and that the latter is not a natural consequence of the former, but should rather be planned institutionally. This Master’s is a proud partner of the International Labour Organisation (ILO), where students will be able to attend lectures and seminars run by ILO officials.

Objectives This international Master’s aims to meet the needs of the global economic world, as well as needs which are not just based on the training of high-level professional managerial figures employed in institutional environments and at private companies working at an international level, but also on the training of new professional figures, such as: social accountability advisors, new market developers, network management experts and international development cooperation experts. This international Master’s is aimed at, in particular, people with roles of responsibility who wish to improve their own skills and, consequently, their own professional status, becoming more competitive in the labour market.

－－－－－－－－－

Duration and summary of training activities and training credits (CFU) The Master's Programme lasts one year and comprises 318-hours of teaching. A 300-hours internship forms an integral part of the course and, as such, an excellent future job opportunity. However, internships for students who are already gainfully employed is facultative or can be supplanted by targeted project work. 1650-hours for a total of 66 CFUs are given over to study, including individual study and the preparation of a final thesis.

Qualification awarded Students who have attended the classes, performed the work placement and written the final thesis will be awarded a level I Master’s Degree in Global Economics and Social Affairs (GESAM). This qualification provides 48 credits towards enrolment onto the post-graduate degree course in Comparative International Relations at the Ca’ Foscari University (www.unive.it/cdl/lm6).

Course period January 2017 > January 2018

Teaching schedule Intensive period of lectures from 16/01/2017 to 03/03/2017, full time from Monday to Friday between 9:00 am and 6:00 pm*

－－－－－－－－－－－－

Attendance Attendance will be monitored by signing a register. The qualification will only be awarded with an attendance of at least 80% of the overall hours (including the total lecture hours and the total work placement/project work hours) and with submission of the thesis, which will be assessed by the Scientific Committee.

Course location Ca’ Foscari – Venice and the ILO – Geneva

Admission requirements FIRST LEVEL /pre-reform university Degree/Diploma /Three-year Degree /Equivalent foreign university qualification in a similar subject, subject to approval from the Teachers’ Board /Certified knowledge of English

Date 2022-02-01

1. Scholarship Application

Please refer to the Scholarship Regulations for detailed information. Application forms should be prepared by applicants and must include academic performance, academic publications, participation in academic activities, participation in Institute activities and other special contributions, as well as an official transcript.

Eligible applicants: First-year and second-year master’s students. Please submit all required documents to the Institute Office by 12:00 noon on March 18. Late submissions will not be accepted.

2. Thesis Title Submission

Thesis titles for the second semester of the 2021–2022 academic year may be submitted from now until June 15, 2022.

3. Oral Examination Application and Completion Deadline

The application deadline for oral examinations is June 9, 2022. The oral examination must be completed by July 7, 2022.

In accordance with the University’s revised Regulations for Graduate Degree Examinations (2019), all theses must undergo similarity checking through the University’s plagiarism detection system. The similarity index shall be reviewed by the advisor, and approval from the advisor is required before applying for the degree examination. It is recommended that the similarity index be below 20%, excluding quotations and references. This standard has been implemented since August 1, 2019. For details on the Turnitin system, please refer to the Institute website.

4. Research Room Application

Application period: February 14 to February 25, 2022. The list of approved users will be announced by March 1, 2022.

Usage period: From March 1, 2022 to the end of July 2022.

Regulations and application forms: Please refer to the “Regulations” and “Downloads” sections on the Institute website.

Students who used the research rooms in the first semester must vacate the rooms and return the keys to the Institute Office by February 25, 2022.

5. Locker Application

Application period: February 14 to February 25, 2022. The list of approved users will be announced by March 1, 2022.

Usage period: From March 1, 2022 to the end of July 2022.

Application procedure: Please register directly at the Institute Office.

Students who used lockers in the first semester must empty the lockers and return the keys to the Institute Office by February 25, 2022.

6. Registration for Research Assistantship Programs

Information regarding registration for research assistantship programs for this semester will be announced after discussion among the faculty of the Institute.

Date 2022-09-01

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Graduate Institute of Labor Research primarily appoints research assistants and provides stipends in order to:

encourage students to complete their master’s theses in a timely manner,

promote student participation in academic activities,

support student involvement in research, and

encourage the publication of research成果.

Full-time faculty members of the Institute determine their own recruitment plans and quotas. An additional position is provided to assist with editorial work for the NCCU Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative affairs of the Institute are mainly supported by part-time assistants employed under labor-based contracts. For specific activities—such as admissions examinations, alumni events, and large-scale events—temporary assistants may be hired on a daily wage basis, with salary and labor insurance handled accordingly.

Note: Recruitment plans and quotas for research assistants are determined by individual faculty members. Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective student assistants in advance, and appointments shall be made upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Recruitment of Research Assistants

Available positions for this semester:

Prof. Chang-Chi Chang: 5 positions (2 for first-year master’s students; 3 for second- and third-year master’s students)

Prof. Tzu-Hui Wu: 2 positions

Other faculty members will arrange their own recruitment plans without announcement by the Institute Office

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information on faculty recruitment plans. (Appendix 1)

Application procedure:

Students who have confirmed participation in a faculty member’s research assistantship plan and will begin implementation this month must, by September 30, jointly complete the NCCU Research Assistant Application Form (Forms 1 and 2) and the Agreement on Intellectual Property Rights for Research Outcomes (Form 3; not required for those not participating in faculty research projects), and submit them to the Institute Office for registration.

Upon completion of the program, the Research Assistant Performance Evaluation Form (Form 4) must be submitted to the Institute Office by January 31, 2023.

Stipend disbursement:

	Stipends will be distributed either monthly or in a lump sum at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan. The amount will be based on the stipend specified in the implementation plan, and the disbursement schedule will follow the University’s reimbursement procedures.

Date 2021-09-01

The following are important announcements for the first semester of Academic Year 2021–2022:

1. Scholarship Applications

Please refer to the Scholarship Regulations for further details.

	Application forms should be prepared by applicants and must include academic performance, academic publications, participation in activities, and an original copy of the transcript.

Eligible applicants: first-year and second-year master’s students.

	Please submit all required documents to the Institute Office by 12:00 PM on September 30, 2021.

	Late submissions will not be accepted.

During the first two weeks of the semester, all courses will be conducted online.

	Students who do not come to campus during this period may submit application documents via email to the Institute Office (labor@nccu.edu.tw).

	The email subject line should be formatted as:

	"Scholarship Application, Fall Semester 2021 – Name – Student ID".

2. Thesis Title Submission

Thesis titles for the first semester of Academic Year 2021–2022 should be submitted from now until December 15, 2021.

3. Oral Defense Application and Completion Deadline

The application deadline for oral defense is December 15, 2021.

	Students must complete their oral defense before January 7, 2022.

In accordance with the University’s revised Guidelines for Graduate Degree Examinations (2019), an additional requirement has been introduced for thesis submission:

	all theses must undergo review through the University’s thesis originality detection system.

The Institute’s review standard is as follows:

	the overall similarity index will be reviewed by the thesis advisor, and only with the advisor’s approval may the student proceed with the degree examination.

	It is recommended that the similarity index be below 20%. Citations and references may be excluded from the evaluation.

This policy has been in effect since August 1, 2019.

	For instructions on using the system, please refer to the relevant guidelines on the Institute’s website.

4. Research Room Applications

Application Period:

	September 13 – September 30, 2021

	The list of approved users will be announced by October 1, 2021.

Usage Period:

	From October 1, 2021 to the end of January 2022.

Regulations and Application Forms:

	Please refer to the relevant regulations and the Download Section on the Institute’s website.

Students who used research rooms in the second semester of Academic Year 2020–2021 must clear out their belongings and return the keys to the Institute Office by September 24, 2021.

During the first two weeks of the semester, all courses will be conducted online.

	Students who do not come to campus during this period may submit application documents via email to the Institute Office (labor@nccu.edu.tw).

	The email subject line should be formatted as:

	"Research Room Application, Fall Semester 2021 – Name – Student ID".

5. Locker Applications

Application Period:

	September 13 – September 30, 2021

	The list of approved users will be announced by October 1, 2021.

Usage Period:

	From October 1, 2021 to the end of January 2022.

Application Method:

	Please register directly at the Institute Office.

Students who used lockers in the second semester of Academic Year 2020–2021 must empty their lockers and return the keys to the Institute Office by September 24, 2021.

During the first two weeks of the semester, all courses will be conducted online.

	Students who do not come to campus during this period may submit application information via email to the Institute Office (labor@nccu.edu.tw).

	The email subject line should be formatted as:

	"Locker Application, Fall Semester 2021 – Name – Student ID".

	The email should include the following information: name, student ID, whether the student has a research room, whether the student has a dormitory assignment, and the locker number from the previous semester (if applicable).

6. Registration for Research Assistant Programs

Information regarding registration for research assistant programs for this semester will be announced separately after faculty members have completed their discussions.

Date 2022-07-13

Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor position

Graduate Institute of Labor Research, National Chengchi University, Taiwan

2022 Job Announcement

 

The Graduate Institute of Labor Research (GILR) at National Chengchi University seeks applications for a Tenure-Track position of Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor with primary expertise in the fields of Human Resource Management, Labor Policy, Labor Relations and Industrial Policy.

 

Qualification of candidates includes a Ph.D degree, at least the assistant professor certificate issued by the Ministry of Education of Taiwan and 4 years of research and teach experience.

 

Successful candidate for this tenure-track position is expected to teach a variety of courses in the following fields (in Chinese and English) :

 

Graduate courses: Human Resource Management, Labor Policy, Labor Relations or Industrial Policy. Practical course in Human Resource Management is preferred.

 

Undergraduate general education courses: Human Resource Management, Labor Policy, Labor Relations or Industrial Policy.

 

Position begins on February 1, 2023

 

Please submit:

 

1. Curriculum Vitae (indicating academic experiences, specializations, research interests, and the rank of position you apply for.)

2. The university teacher certificate issued by the Ministry of Education, Taiwan (Assistant Professor level or above)

3. Certificate of PhD degree 

4. List of publications.

5. PhD dissertation and up to five representative publications from the last 5 years. (Applicants with associate professor level or above, do not need to submit their PhD dissertation.)

6. Four syllabi of courses (including one in English and three in Chinese) you intend to teach.

 

Please send one electronic copy of the aforementioned documents (1-6) to [labor@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:labor@nccu.edu.tw).

 

Please also send five hard copy to the GILR, addressed:

Graduate Institute of Labor Research

National Chengchi University

12th Floor, South Wing, General Building of Colleges, No. 64, Sec. 2, ZhiNan Rd., Wenshan District, Taipei 11605, Taiwan

 

*postmarked by September 20, 2022, and sent to the GILR by registered mail.

 

Application materials must be received by the GILR no later than September 20, 2022 (Thursday).

 

Candidate after document review, will if necessary be invited to give a talk scheduled in between October 07 and November 07, 2022.

 

If you have any inquiries, please contact Ms Chen at 886-2-2938-7108 or labor@nccu.edu.tw

[Tenure-Track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor position in GILR, NCCU](https://labor.nccu.edu.tw/PageDocAll/upload/45/doc/17112/Tenure-Track position in GILR, NCCU.pdf)

Date 2022-04-10

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Graduate Institute of Labor Research primarily appoints research assistants and provides stipends in order to:

encourage students to complete their master’s theses in a timely manner,

promote student participation in academic activities,

support student involvement in research, and

encourage the publication of research成果.

Full-time faculty members of the Institute determine their own recruitment plans and quotas. An additional position is provided to assist with editorial work for the NCCU Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative affairs of the Institute are mainly supported by part-time assistants employed under labor-based contracts. For specific activities—such as admissions examinations, alumni events, and large-scale events—temporary assistants may be hired on a daily wage basis, with salary and labor insurance handled accordingly.

Note: Recruitment plans and quotas for research assistants are determined by individual faculty members. Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective student assistants in advance, and appointments shall be made upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Recruitment of Research Assistants

Available positions for this semester:

Prof. Chang-Chi Chang: 5 positions (2 for first-year master’s students; 3 for second- and third-year master’s students)

Prof. Tzu-Hui Wu: 2 positions

Other faculty members will arrange their own recruitment plans without announcement by the Institute Office

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information on faculty recruitment plans. (Appendix 1)

Application procedure:

Students who have confirmed participation in a faculty member’s research assistantship plan and will begin implementation this month must, by April 30, jointly complete the NCCU Research Assistant Application Form (Forms 1 and 2) and the Agreement on Intellectual Property Rights for Research Outcomes (Form 3; not required for those not participating in faculty research projects), and submit them to the Institute Office for registration.

Upon completion of the program, the Research Assistant Performance Evaluation Form (Form 4) must be submitted to the Institute Office by July 31, 2022.

Stipend disbursement:

	Stipends will be distributed either monthly or in a lump sum at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan. The amount will be based on the stipend specified in the implementation plan, and the disbursement schedule will follow the University’s reimbursement procedures.

Date 2022-09-01

1. Scholarship Application

Please refer to the Scholarship Regulations for detailed information. Application forms should be prepared by applicants and must include academic performance, academic publications, participation in academic activities, participation in Institute activities and other special contributions, as well as an official transcript.

Eligible applicants: First-year and second-year master’s students. Please submit all required documents to the Institute Office by 12:00 noon on October 3. Late submissions will not be accepted.

2. Thesis Title Submission

Thesis titles for the first semester of the 2022–2023 academic year may be submitted from now until December 15, 2022.

3. Oral Examination Application and Completion Deadline

The application deadline for oral examinations is December 22, 2022. The oral examination must be completed by January 7, 2023.

4. Research Room Application

Application period: September 12 to September 23, 2022. The list of approved users will be announced by September 26, 2022.

Usage period: From September 26, 2022 to the end of January 2023.

Regulations and application forms: Please refer to the “Regulations” and “Downloads” sections on the Institute website.

Students who used the research rooms in the second semester of the 2021–2022 academic year must vacate the rooms and return the keys to the Institute Office by September 23, 2022.

5. Locker Application

Application period: September 12 to September 23, 2022. The list of approved users will be announced by September 26, 2022.

Usage period: From September 26, 2022 to the end of January 2023.

Application procedure: Please register directly at the Institute Office.

Students who used lockers in the second semester of the 2021–2022 academic year must empty the lockers and return the keys to the Institute Office by September 23, 2022.

6. Registration for Research Assistantship Programs

Information regarding registration for research assistantship programs for this semester will be announced after discussion among the faculty of the Institute.

Date 2024-08-12

Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor position 

Graduate Institute of Labor Research, National Chengchi University, Taiwan

2024 Job Announcement

 

The Graduate Institute of Labor Research (GILR) at National Chengchi University seeks applications for a Tenure-Track position of Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor with primary expertise in the fields of Sociology of Work, Social Security and Work-related Sustainability.

 

Qualification of candidates includes a Ph.D degree, at least the assistant professor certificate issued by the Ministry of Education of Taiwan and 1 years of research and teach experience.

 

Successful candidate for this tenure-track position is expected to teach a variety of courses in the following fields (in Chinese and English) :

 

Graduate courses: Sociology of Work, Social Security and Work-related Sustainability. Practical course in Sociology of Work is preferred.

 

Undergraduate general education courses: Sociology of Work, Social Security and Work-related Sustainability.

 

Position begins on February 1, 2025

 

Please submit:

1. Curriculum Vitae (indicating academic experiences, specializations, research interests, and the rank of position you apply for.)

2. The university teacher certificate issued by the Ministry of Education, Taiwan (Assistant Professor level or above)

3. Certificate of PhD degree 

4. List of publications.

5. PhD dissertation and up to five representative publications from the last 5 years. (Applicants with associate professor level or above, do not need to submit their PhD dissertation.)

6. Four syllabi of courses (including one in English and three in Chinese) you intend to teach.

 

Please send one electronic copy of the aforementioned documents (1-6) to [labor@nccu.edu.tw](mailto:labor@nccu.edu.tw). The applicants should clearly mark “Applying for the faculty position in GILR, NCCU”.

 

Please also send five hard copy to the GILR, addressed:

Graduate Institute of Labor Research

National Chengchi University

12th Floor, South Wing, General Building of Colleges, No. 64, Sec. 2, ZhiNan Rd., Wenshan District, Taipei 11605, Taiwan

 

*postmarked by October 15, 2024, and sent to the GILR by registered mail.

 

Application materials must be received by the GILR no later than October 15, 2024 (Tuesday).

 

Candidate after document review, will if necessary be invited to give a talk scheduled in between November 07 and November 14, 2024.

 

If you have any inquiries, please contact Ms Chen at 886-2-2938-7108 or labor@nccu.edu.tw

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Graduate Institute of Labor Research primarily appoints research assistants and provides stipends in order to:

encourage students to complete their master’s theses in a timely manner,

promote student participation in academic activities,

support student involvement in research, and

encourage the publication of research成果.

Full-time faculty members of the Institute determine their own recruitment plans and quotas. An additional position is provided to assist with editorial work for the NCCU Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative affairs of the Institute are mainly supported by part-time assistants employed under labor-based contracts. For specific activities—such as admissions examinations, alumni events, and large-scale events—temporary assistants may be hired on a daily wage basis, with salary and labor insurance handled accordingly.

Note: Recruitment plans and quotas for research assistants are determined by individual faculty members. Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective student assistants in advance, and appointments shall be made upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Recruitment of Research Assistants

Available positions for this semester:

Prof. Chou-Kang Chiu: 3 positions

Prof. Tzu-Hui Wu: 2 positions

Other faculty members will arrange their own recruitment plans without announcement by the Institute Office

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information on faculty recruitment plans. (Appendix 1)

Application procedure:

Students who have confirmed participation in a faculty member’s research assistantship plan and will begin implementation this month must, by May 31, jointly complete the NCCU Research Assistant Application Form (Forms 1 and 2) and the Agreement on Intellectual Property Rights for Research Outcomes (Form 3; not required for those not participating in faculty research projects), and submit them to the Institute Office for registration.

Upon completion of the program, the Research Assistant Performance Evaluation Form (Form 4) must be submitted to the Institute Office by July 31, 2023.

Stipend disbursement:

	Stipends will be distributed either monthly or in a lump sum at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan. The amount will be based on the stipend specified in the implementation plan, and the disbursement schedule will follow the University’s reimbursement procedures.

1. Amount of the Scholarship

The scholarship provides up to NTD 30,000 per recipient.

2. Eligibility and Quota

One recipient will be selected each academic year.

Applicants must be currently enrolled master’s students of the Graduate Institute of Labor Research.

3. Application Requirements

Applicants must participate in overseas study or exchange programs and submit a project proposal.

Applicants must have an average academic grade of at least 80 in the previous semester.

Priority will be given to applicants who meet the above criteria and come from low-income or middle-to-low-income households, financially disadvantaged backgrounds, or single-parent families, with supporting documents provided.

4. Application Deadline

From now until March 6, 2023.

Please submit all required documents to the Institute Office.

5. Required Documents

Scholarship application form (please refer to the attached application guidelines).

One copy of the previous semester’s academic transcript.

Proposal for the overseas study or exchange program.

Supporting documents for low-income, middle-to-low-income, or financially disadvantaged status (if applicable).

Any additional supporting documents for review (optional).

6. Review Process

The scholarship will be reviewed by the Scholarship Review Committee established by the Graduate Institute of Labor Research.

The committee consists of full-time faculty members of the Institute.

Final decisions will be approved by the Director of the Institute, and recipients will be notified individually. No public announcement will be made.

Date 2023-10-03

Speech Topic:

Local articulation of Global Framework Agreements in the Global South

Speaker:

Prof. Santanu Sarkar, labour relations and HRM at XLRI Xavier School of Management in India

Date: 

Oct 11, 2023 Wed 12:10~14:00

Venue:

Third Meeting Room, 12F, General Building (South wing), National Chengchi University

Online Registration:

[https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScZE3th3cT3Cbl03_uKumX3PggXhmDyU7hs4QRjRGD8elFuNA/viewform](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScZE3th3cT3Cbl03_uKumX3PggXhmDyU7hs4QRjRGD8elFuNA/viewform)

Registration deadline:

Oct 06, 2023

Abstract:

The global operations of multinational companies have affected a large number of workers around the world. Global Framework Agreements (GFAs) are intended to protect such workers. Prof. Santanu will take India as an example to introduce the actual implementation and achievements of three GFAs signed by three German multinational companies in india (Siemens, Bosch, Daimler), with IG Metall, IMF and IndustriALL. We will also examine the role played by labor unions in order to see whether GFAs are a labor protection mechanism that the international community can expect.

Note:

Lunch box will be provided at this event

Date 2019-09-01

The following are important announcements for the first semester of Academic Year 2019–2020:

1. Scholarship Applications

Please refer to the Scholarship Regulations for further details.

	Application forms should be prepared by applicants and must include academic performance, academic publications, participation in activities, and an original copy of the transcript.

Eligible applicants: first-year and second-year master’s students.

	Please submit all required documents to the Institute Office by 12:00 PM on September 30, 2019.

	Late submissions will not be accepted.

2. Thesis Title Submission

Thesis titles for the first semester of Academic Year 2019–2020 should be submitted from now until December 15, 2019.

3. Oral Defense Application and Completion Deadline

The application deadline for oral defense is December 15, 2019.

	Students must complete their oral defense before January 7, 2020.

In accordance with the University’s revised Guidelines for Graduate Degree Examinations (2019), an additional requirement has been introduced for thesis submission:

	all theses must undergo review through the University’s plagiarism detection system.

The Institute’s review standard for thesis similarity is as follows:

	the overall similarity index will be reviewed by the thesis advisor, and only with the advisor’s approval may the student proceed with the degree examination.

	It is recommended that the similarity index be below 20%. Citations and references may be excluded from the evaluation.

This policy has been in effect since August 1, 2019.

	For instructions on using the plagiarism detection system, please refer to the relevant guidelines on the Institute’s website.

4. Research Room Applications

Application Period:

	September 9 – September 20, 2019

	The list of approved users will be announced by September 23, 2019.

Usage Period:

	From September 23, 2019 to the end of January 2020.

Regulations and Application Forms:

	Please refer to the relevant regulations and the Download Section on the Institute’s website.

Students who used research rooms in the second semester of Academic Year 2018–2019 must clear out their belongings and return the keys to the Institute Office by September 20, 2019.

5. Locker Applications

Application Period:

	September 9 – September 20, 2019

	The list of approved users will be announced by September 23, 2019.

Usage Period:

	From September 23, 2019 to the end of January 2020.

Application Method:

	Please register directly at the Institute Office.

Students who used lockers in the second semester of Academic Year 2018–2019 must empty their lockers and return the keys to the Institute Office by September 20, 2019.

6. Registration for Part-time Assistants

Information regarding registration for part-time assistants for this semester will be announced separately after faculty members have completed their discussions.

Date 2021-01-29

Graduate Institute of Labor Research, National Chengchi University, Taiwan

2021 Job Announcement

The Graduate Institute of Labor Research (GILR) at National Chengchi University seeks applications for a Tenure-Track position of Assistant Professor/Associate Professor/Professor with primary expertise in the fields of Labor Law, Labor Relations, Social Security and Human Resources.

Qualified candidates must have a Ph.D degree, at least the Assistant Professor certificate and also 4 years of researching and teaching experience.

Successful candidate for this tenure-track position is expected to teach a variety of courses in the following fields (in Chinese and English).

Graduate courses: Labor Law, Labor Relations, Social Security or Human Resources. Practical course in Labor Law is preferred.

Undergraduate general education courses: Labor Law, Labor Relations, Social Security or Human Resources.

Position begins on August 1, 2021

Please submit:

1. Curriculum Vitae (indicating academic experiences, specializations, research interests, and the rank of position you apply for.)

2. The university teacher certificate (Assistant Professor or above)

3. Certificate of PhD degree 

4. List of publications.

5. PhD dissertation and up to five representative publications from the last 5 years.

6. Four syllabi of courses (including two in English and three in Chinese) you intend to teach.

Please send one electronic copy of the aforementioned documents (1-6) to labor@nccu.edu.tw.

Please also send five hard copy to the GILR, addressed:

Graduate Institute of Labor Research

National Chengchi University

12th Floor, South Wing, General Building of Colleges, No. 64, Sec. 2, ZhiNan Rd., Wenshan District, Taipei 11605, Taiwan

*postmarked by March 31, 2021, and sent to the GILR by registered mail.

Application materials must be received by the GILR no later than March 31, 2021 (Wednesday).

Candidate after document review, will if necessary be invited to give a talk scheduled in between April 06 and April 23, 2021.

If you have any inquiries, please contact Ms Chen at 886-2-2938-7108 or labor@nccu.edu.tw

Date 2020-09-01

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Institute primarily appoints research assistants (graduate student assistants) and provides stipends in order to:

encourage students to complete their master’s theses in a timely manner,

support participation in academic activities,

facilitate involvement in research activities,

and encourage the publication of research outcomes.

Appointment plans and quotas are determined independently by full-time faculty members.

	One additional position is allocated for assisting with editorial work for the Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative duties of the Institute are primarily supported by labor-based part-time assistants.

	For specific activities such as admissions examinations, alumni events, and large-scale events, temporary labor-based part-time assistants may be hired on a daily employment basis, with compensation and labor insurance handled accordingly.

Supplementary Note:

	The appointment plans and quotas for research assistants are determined by individual faculty members.

	Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective student assistants in advance, and appointments shall be made only upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Appointment of Research Assistants

Available Positions for Registration (This Semester):

Prof. Chang-Chi Chang: 4 positions (2 for first-year students; 2 for second-year students)

Other faculty members will arrange their own plans independently without announcement through the Institute Office.

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information on faculty-specific plans (Attachment 1).

Application Procedure:

Students who have been confirmed to participate in a faculty member’s research assistant plan and will begin implementation this month should, together with their supervising faculty member, complete the Learning Relationship Recognition Form (Form 1) and the Learning Activity Plan (Form 2), and submit them to the Institute Office for registration by September 30, 2020.

After completing the plan for this semester, the Learning Outcome Evaluation Form (Form 3) should be submitted to the Institute Office by January 31, 2021.

Stipend Disbursement:

	The Institute Office will disburse stipends either on a monthly basis or as a lump sum at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan.

	The amount will be based on the stipend specified in the Learning Activity Plan, and the disbursement schedule will follow the University’s accounting procedures.

Date 2020-04-01

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Institute primarily appoints research assistants (graduate student assistants) and provides stipends in order to:

encourage students to complete their master’s theses in a timely manner,

support participation in academic activities,

facilitate involvement in research activities, and

encourage the publication of research outcomes.

Appointment plans and quotas are determined independently by full-time faculty members.

	One additional position is allocated for assisting with editorial work for the Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative duties of the Institute are primarily supported by labor-based part-time assistants.

	For specific activities such as admissions examinations, alumni events, and large-scale events, temporary labor-based part-time assistants may be hired on a daily employment basis, with compensation and labor insurance handled accordingly.

Supplementary Note:

	The appointment plans and quotas for research assistants are determined by individual faculty members.

	Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective student assistants in advance, and appointments shall be made only upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Appointment of Research Assistants

Available Positions for Registration (This Semester):

Prof. Chang-Chi Chang: 4 positions (2 for first-year students; 2 for second-year students)

Other faculty members will arrange their own plans independently without announcement through the Institute Office.

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information on faculty-specific plans (Attachment 1).

Application Procedure:

Students who have been confirmed to participate in a faculty member’s research assistant plan and will begin implementation this month should, together with their supervising faculty member, complete the Learning Relationship Recognition Form (Form 1) and the Learning Activity Plan (Form 2), and submit them to the Institute Office for registration by April 6, 2020.

After completing the plan for this semester, the Learning Outcome Evaluation Form (Form 3) should be submitted to the Institute Office by July 31, 2020.

Stipend Disbursement:

	The Institute Office will disburse stipends either on a monthly basis or as a lump sum at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan.

	The amount will be based on the stipend specified in the Learning Activity Plan, and the disbursement schedule will follow the University’s accounting procedures.

The following are important announcements for the first semester of Academic Year 2017–2018:

Please refer to the Scholarship Regulations for further details.

	Application forms should be prepared by applicants and must include academic performance, academic publications, participation in activities, and an original copy of the transcript.

Eligible applicants: first-year and second-year master’s students.

	Please submit all required documents to the Institute Office by 12:00 PM on September 29, 2017.

	Late submissions will not be accepted.

2. Thesis Title Submission

Thesis titles for the first semester of Academic Year 2017–2018 should be submitted from now until December 15, 2017.

3. Oral Defense Application and Completion Deadline

The application deadline for oral defense is December 15, 2017.

Students must complete their oral defense before the first week of January 2018.

	From September 26, 2017 to the end of January 2018.

Date 2017-10-01

1. Principles for the Appointment of Part-time Assistants

In accordance with University regulations, the Institute primarily appoints research assistants (graduate student assistants) and provides stipends in order to:

encourage students to complete their master’s theses in a timely manner,

support participation in academic activities,

facilitate involvement in research activities, and

encourage the publication of research outcomes.

Appointment plans and quotas are determined independently by full-time faculty members.

	One additional position is allocated for assisting with editorial work for the Journal of Labor Studies.

Administrative duties of the Institute are primarily supported by labor-based part-time assistants.

	For specific activities such as admissions examinations, alumni events, and large-scale events, temporary labor-based part-time assistants may be hired on a daily employment basis, with compensation and labor insurance handled accordingly.

Supplementary Note:

	The appointment plans and quotas for research assistants are determined by individual faculty members.

	Faculty members should explain relevant regulations to prospective student assistants in advance, and appointments shall be made only upon mutual agreement.

2. Information on the Appointment of Research Assistants

Available Positions for Registration (This Semester):

Prof. Hui-Ling Wang: 1 position

Prof. Chih-Yueh Cheng: 2 positions

Prof. Chang-Chi Chang: 4 positions

Other faculty members will arrange their own plans independently without announcement through the Institute Office.

Eligibility:

	Please refer to the attached table for detailed information on faculty-specific plans (Attachment 1).

Application Procedure:

	Students who have been confirmed to participate in a faculty member’s research assistant plan and will begin implementation this month should, together with their supervising faculty member, complete the required forms (Learning Relationship Recognition Form and Learning Activity Plan) and submit them to the Institute Office for registration by October 27, 2017.

Stipend Disbursement:

	The Institute Office will disburse stipends either on a monthly basis or as a lump sum at the end of the semester, depending on the faculty member’s plan.

	The amount will be based on the stipend specified in the Learning Activity Plan, and the disbursement schedule will follow the University’s accounting procedures.

Date 2017-10-01

The Division of International Education under the Office of International Cooperation is accepting applications for the International Student Scholarship (General Scholarship) for the first semester of Academic Year 2017–2018 from now until October 31, 2017.

1. Eligibility

This scholarship is open to international students who have been enrolled at the University for at least one semester.

Exchange students and students who are already receiving other full scholarships are not eligible to apply.

2. Application Procedure

Applicants must complete the following steps by October 31, 2017:

Complete the online application at: [https://goo.gl/uASVMm](https://goo.gl/uASVMm)

Submit the following documents via email to the Office of International Cooperation(alison@nccu.edu.tw)

One copy of the official Chinese transcript, including grades from the second semester of Academic Year 2016–2017

		(students writing a thesis must additionally submit a study/research proposal)

Proof of volunteer service contributing to the internationalization of the University and the local community

		(please refer to the attached format)

Supporting documents for club participation or extracurricular activities (optional)

3. Additional Information

Please refer to the Regulations Governing the Application for the Ministry of Education International Student Scholarship for further details.

場次一

主持人：中川純教授、王惠玲教授

103年10月15日(三)

場次一

場次三

主題：就業促進與僱用保障

場次四

主題：勞動經濟與產業關係

主持人：中研院經濟研究所研究員江豐富教授

發表人：會長蘇海南、研究員馬小麗、副教授喬健、謝棋楠教授、孟續鐸研究員、劉唐宇副教授、羅丹

發表人：潘淑貞副教授、王正慧助理教授、嚴佳代研究員、林麒瑋記者、林燦螢助理教授、蕭靜芬、鍾珮珊、黃同圳教授、張秋蘭助理教授、黃敏雯、劉仲矩教授、劉諺咨、姚瑋、陳儀蓉副教授、程邦雲

評述人：鄭仁偉教授、陳澤義教授、林燦螢助理教授

場次六

主題：人力發展與職業教育訓練

主持人：中國人民大學勞動人事學院副院長劉爾鐸副教授

發表人：林大鈞副教授、王健、林燦螢助理教授、羅啟誠、白景文助理教授、郭沛軒、宋敏、馬康康、陳宏壽、韓燁

評述人：徐廣正副教授、劉梅君教授、王安祥教授

主辦單位 ：

			中華勞動與就業關係協會

共同主辦單位 ：

			臺灣地區：臺灣海峽兩岸法律交流協會

			大陸地區：中國勞動學會

			香港地區：香港人力資源管理學會

			澳門地區：澳門人力資源協會

協辦單位

學術合辦單位 ：

			臺灣地區：財團法人國家政策研究基金會、文化大學勞工關係系所、中正大學勞工關係系所、政治大學勞工研究所

其他合辦單位 ：中華勞促會

一、本所兼任助理進用原則

本所按學校相關規定，採進用研究獎助生方式支給助學金為主，以鼓勵學生儘速研撰並完成碩士論文、鼓勵學生協助或參與學術活動、協助學生參與或從事研究活動、鼓勵學生發表研究成果，本所專任教師自行訂定方案與名額，並額外增加一位協助勞動學報編務。

本所所務行政事宜以進用勞動型兼任助理為主，其他部分如招生考試支援、校友返校活動、大型活動等特定活動，必要時進用勞動型臨時性兼任助理，並以「日僱型」處理其薪資與勞健保事宜。

附帶說明：研究獎助生方案與名額由本所專任教師自訂，教師應事前與有意擔任研究獎助生之學生說明相關規定，雙方合意方得擔任。

二、研究獎助生進用相關資訊

1.本學期研究獎助生開放登記名額：丘周剛老師開放3名登記，其他老師擬自行規劃方案，不透過所辦公告。

2.研究獎助生進用資格：請參見下頁表格本所老師方案規劃相關資訊。（附件1）

3.研究獎助生進用方式：

（1）確認擔任上述老師方案的研究獎助生，並於本月起執行方案者，請於10/31前與所屬老師共同填寫國立政治大學研究獎助生申請表（表1+2）、研究獎助生相關研究成果著作權與專利權之歸屬約定書（表3，無參與老師研究計畫者可免填），並送交所辦登記。

（2）待本學期方案執行完畢，研究獎助生學習成效評量表（表4）請於114/01/31前送交所辦登記。

4.研究獎助生助學金發放方式：所辦將分別依照老師方案，每月底定期性或學期末一次性發放助學金，發放金額以學習活動實施計畫所註記之助學金金額為準，發放日期將配合學校結報日期辦理。

「長期照護保險之政策需求與制度規劃」系列演講-活動簡介

1883 年，德國實施健康保險，並於 6 年內接連實施勞災保險及年金保險，開啟了社會保險的序幕。1927 年，德國實施失業保險，而形成社會保險的四大支柱。

  德國的社會保險，不止擴及東西歐各國，美洲國家也隨之跟進，其中，尤以美國 1935 年社會安全法案所實施的年金保險最具指標性。在亞洲，日本是社會保險的先驅。台灣、南韓，繼之。如今台灣也已健康、年金、失業及勞災保險兼具。台灣的醫療在各國評比中，每名列前矛，甚且居冠，成功的健保，是極為重要的因素。台灣的勞保年金，以不到 20 年時間將退休年齡由 60 提升至 65，並實施延退優惠方案，則是各國年金改革的重要典範。社會保險，起於德國，擴及全世界，進而得到人權宣言及經社文人權公約的肯認，而成為普世價值。

  有鑑於人口老化所帶來長期照護需求，不是既有社會保險可以涵蓋並承擔，德國於 1980 年代開始積極規劃長期照護保險，並於 1995 年完成立法並實施。社會保險，因以具有五大支柱。其後，日本於公元 2000 年隨即跟進，南韓亦於 2008 年再跟進。

  如今，台灣亦面臨人口老化的社會變遷，長期照護也成了社會的問題與議題。面對此等社會遽變，當如何因應，成為時代的任務與挑戰。德國的長期照護保險是重要的選項。如果不採，有其它方案？如果要採行，當有何等規劃進程與內容？

  為此，德國是長期照護保險制度，最為重要的實驗室，當深入認識並研究。其它國家，歐洲跟進實施的奧地利、法國、西班牙及比利時荷語區，以及亞洲的日本、南韓，都具有高度參考價值。

  基於前述社會背景以及政策、制度規劃之需求，特舉辦此演講系列，共三場次，活動細節如下，廣邀學術界及實務界共襄盛舉

一、本所兼任助理進用原則

本所按學校相關規定，採進用研究獎助生方式支給助學金為主，以鼓勵學生儘速研撰並完成碩士論文、鼓勵學生協助或參與學術活動、協助學生參與或從事研究活動、鼓勵學生發表研究成果，本所專任教師自行訂定方案與名額，並額外增加一位協助勞動學報編務。

本所所務行政事宜以進用勞動型兼任助理為主，其他部分如招生考試支援、校友返校活動、大型活動等特定活動，必要時進用勞動型臨時性兼任助理，並以「日僱型」處理其薪資與勞健保事宜。

附帶說明：研究獎助生方案與名額由本所專任教師自訂，教師應事前與有意擔任研究獎助生之學生說明相關規定，雙方合意方得擔任。

二、研究獎助生進用相關資訊

1.本學期研究獎助生開放登記名額：丘周剛老師開放3名登記，其他老師擬自行規劃方案，不透過所辦公告。

2.研究獎助生進用資格：請參見下頁表格本所老師方案規劃相關資訊。（附件1）

3.研究獎助生進用方式：

（1）確認擔任上述老師方案的研究獎助生，並於本月起執行方案者，請於05/31前與所屬老師共同填寫國立政治大學研究獎助生申請表（表1+2）、研究獎助生相關研究成果著作權與專利權之歸屬約定書（表3，無參與老師研究計畫者可免填），並送交所辦登記。

（2）待本學期方案執行完畢，研究獎助生學習成效評量表（表4）請於113/07/31前送交所辦登記。

4.研究獎助生助學金發放方式：所辦將分別依照老師方案，每月底定期性或學期末一次性發放助學金，發放金額以學習活動實施計畫所註記之助學金金額為準，發放日期將配合學校結報日期辦理。

[演講海報](https://labor.nccu.edu.tw/PageDocAll/upload/45/doc/27601/A1尺寸(0408講座).jpg)

一、題目：從剝削到連帶、從輾壓到奮起－移工築起的地下社會

二、時間：2024.04.08(星期一) 16:10~18:00

三、地點：政大綜合院館南棟二樓270209教室

四、主講人：簡永達 自由記者

五、主持人：政治大學勞工研究所 劉梅君教授

六、報名方式：現場參加

七、主辦單位：政治大學勞工研究所

八、內容簡介：

台灣有超過70萬名移工，他們是底層勞動市場的人力，從農漁、營建、傳統3K產業到科技業，臺灣經濟成長的實績有許多來自他們的血汗與付出。 他們為一個個家庭承擔長照與看護之責，若沒有他們作為補充人力，已是高齡化社會的臺灣將有許多地方難以運作。 當他們出現在公眾視野時，時常顯得扁平、晦暗，連結的意象往往也與剝削、勞動傷害甚或死亡有關……然而，真實的他們，究竟是什麼樣子的呢？ 其實，選擇跨海工作就是面對未知，這些願意來臺工作的異鄉人，正是一群勇於擺脫既定生活、充滿冒險性格的人。當他們碰撞上充滿歧視的移工制度與僵固法律，有些不幸遭致碾壓，但也有許多人展現了高度能動性，在制度所不及之處，以各自的方法與想像，和臺灣這塊土地產生連結，建構起屬於他們自身的連帶、社群與地下社會。

※請碩一同學注意：

關於公部門實習（勞動相關政府部門暑期實習）單位申請，多有制式申請表格並訂有申請期限。

一、申請時間與單位實習公告

按往年慣例，各部門會在4月開始自行在各自的官方網站公布相關訊息，5月中旬截止申請，請有意願前往公部門實習的同學留意相關單位公告。

以下提供實習申請概要給碩一同學參考：(實際情況仍以今年各單位最新公告為主)

1.勞動部：沒有制式申請表與沒有申請截止期限，但有名額限制（先搶先贏，但近年因疫情考量無開放受理實習申請）。本學期（112-2）有意申請勞動部實習的同學，請於2024/4/8（一）前將申請文件繳交所辦，申請文件可參考勞保局文件格式自行修改：[https://www.bli.gov.tw/0016791.html](https://www.bli.gov.tw/0016791.html)。

2.新北市勞工局：沒有制式申請表與申請截止期限，但有名額限制，先搶先贏。

3.台北市勞動局：沒有制式申請表但有名額限制，先搶先贏(按以往大多於每年5月1日至5月18日期間受理申請)。

4.勞保局：有制式申請表單，2024尚未公告實習計畫，往年實習計畫多於四月中公告，並於五月中申請截止（但近年因疫情考量無開放受理實習申請），有意申請者請逕行留意勞保局公告，文件準備相關細節可先參考2021年「勞動部勞工保險局提供國內各大學院校學生暑期實習計畫」 [https://www.bli.gov.tw/0016791.html](https://www.bli.gov.tw/0016791.html) 。

(1)實習期間：每年暑假辦理1次，原則為4週。

(2)實習學生名額：依勞保局每年實際情形公告。

2024年慈林史料中心實習

 

一、宗旨:

慈林教育基金會為增進基金會與學校之交流合作，使學生能透過實務工作與本會人員進行合作與學習，累積未來發展經驗與資歷。

二、申請資格:

各大專院校學生，博物館學、圖書資訊管理、歷史學、檔案管理、人文社會學科相關領域在學學生優先考量。

對歷史、文化與社會運動有興趣者。若具有相關學科相關背景知識、團隊合作能力、創意思維及溝通協調能力者佳。

對社會運動史料實物或圖書資料整理工作，有濃厚興趣並樂於參與者。

具備高度耐心及細心的特質、電腦打字及文件編輯技能，以及基本的資料處理能力（如搜尋、整理、分類等）和簡易的影音剪輯能力。

能配合本會規定之實習時間，並全程參與者。

三、實習內容：

協助本會社會運動史料、實物或圖書資料整理，資料Key in與建檔、館藏資料盤點與清查等。

發揮創意，並善用本會現有資源，將其整理為可供展覽或推廣之素材，並協助本會執行教育推廣活動，例如特展、社會運動故事短影音等，藉以提高參與者對於相關社會運動主題的認識和瞭解。另外在許可範圍內得參加本會辦理之演講、內部訓練、研習會等課程。

四、申請日期：即日起至2024年5月10日止。

五：需求名額：需求為1-3名。

 

六、聯絡資訊：03-9650515*231 楊小姐

一、投稿說明

本所擬於2024年05月31日（星期五）辦理勞動關係學術研討會，本次學術研討會徵求論文主要以勞動議題為主，舉凡勞動研究相關領域之主題論文，均歡迎各位研究生踴躍投稿，發表論文者皆授與發表證明。

二、徵稿對象

以三校研究生（政治大學、中正大學、文化大學）、畢業生為主，另亦歡迎相關領域之他校研究生投稿。

三、徵稿主題

1. 勞動法令與政策議題

2. 人力資源管理議題

3. 勞動社會議題

4. 勞動經濟議題

四、投稿需知

1. 初稿：需包含發表人基本資料，如姓名、職稱、服務單位、email、連絡電話、論文題目，及500字內的摘要與關鍵字。

2. 完稿：論文應包含研究動機及目的、分析架構、研究方法、主要論點、預期發現，全文字數8000字內。

3. 摘要格式與論文全文格式規定請見附件。

五、相關日期與投遞方式

1. 500字論文摘要截稿日期：2024年04月15日（星期一）

2. 論文摘要審查結果通知日期：2024年05月01日（星期三）

[海報](https://labor.nccu.edu.tw/PageDocAll/upload/45/doc/26763/Untitled.jpg)

一、活動簡介

1938年美國國會通過了一週工作五天的制度，工作五天隨後成為富裕國家普遍共享的制度。八十五年過去了，這套制度從未曾再接受過檢驗，直到新冠疫情爆發。疫情催生了一週工作四天的運動，首先是美國，接著是全球。疫情讓員工承受的工作壓力向上推升，過勞情況變得比以往更為嚴重。部份僱主開始提供降低工時的福利緩解員工身心壓力，而遠距上班的普及也讓工時變得更有彈性；另一個催生因素則是AI的快速發展。現在全球許多政府開始進行工作四天的實驗。2022年初我開始帶領研究團隊針對願意試行工作四天不減薪的企業進行研究。我們的研究不僅顯示員工福祉獲得大幅提升，同時員工工作表現、留任率以及任職率各方面都出現成長。在這個演講中我將討論降低工時運動以及我們的研究成果，包括對環境氣候的影響，並為未來選項提供些反思。歡迎有興趣者報名參加。

【獎學金公告】113年度財團法人法律扶助基金會碩博士論文研究計畫獎助

法律扶助為一跨學科之研究領域，為鼓勵相關研究，促進法律扶助制度發展，本會設有「碩博士論文研究計畫獎助辦法」，獎勵國內公私立大學院校碩博士研究生就法律扶助政策、法規等進行研究。

一、獎助對象：國內公私立大學院校之在學碩博士研究生。但已獲本辦法奬助或其他經費獎（補）助者，不得申請。

二、名額與金額：

博士生一名，新台幣6萬元。 碩士生二名，每名新台幣3萬元。 （實際名額以評審結果為準）

三、研究範圍：

法律扶助制度（如：組織型態、服務範圍、財務、品質控管等）。

本會政策或專案之成效評估。

針對特定弱勢族群的扶助（如：婦女、兒童、原住民、勞工、移民移工、身心障礙者、居住權益、老人、災害受害人等）。

弱勢族群尋求法律服務之行為模式。

科技創新與法律扶助（例如：運用現代科技之服務與其施行成效）。

法律扶助宣導與大眾法治教育。

四、申請方式：113年3月1日起至113年4月30日止（以郵戳為憑），檢具必要文件，向法扶基金會申請。審查結果屆時將公布於基金會官網(https://www.laf.org.tw/)

※有關本獎助之獎助對象、範圍、名額及獎金、申請與審查方式、獎助給付方式、受獎助者相關權利義務與獎助取消之情事等，請詳參本會「碩博士論文研究計畫獎助辦法」。

達方電子人資專員

達方電子上市於2007年，為明基友達集團關係企業，生產的鍵盤為全球前三大，現正積極轉型衝刺綠能等多元事業。2022年集團營收近10億美元（約新台幣300億元），綠能跟IT鍵盤應用，都將成為集團成長的雙引擎。

一、提供的工作內容：

1. 與事業單位合作達成專業人才的招募甄選、諮詢服務、並拓展或優化招募工具。

2. 產學合作與各大學校建立和維護積極的關係(產碩、實習生、校園說明會等)。

3. 規劃或參與HR相關招募專案(雇主品牌建立：如LinkedIn、FB各項活動與專案)。

4. 公司及福委會相關活動之企劃撰寫提案、執行、主持、推廣

5. 其它員工關係綜合業務發展與推動

6. 參與各項人力資源綜合業務發展與推動

二、想在你身上看到的：

1. 大學以上教育、心理、人資、企管等相關系所畢業程度，碩士者佳。

2. 具備500人以上規模製造業或科技業人力資源工作經驗

3. 招募工作經驗1年以上or經營福委會及大型活動企畫統籌相關經驗1年以上

4. 具學校社團活動經驗為佳

5. 具備雇主品牌經營相關經驗佳

6. 【特質要求】

個性活潑、具備同理心，處事正向，擅於溝通應對、團隊合作。

能適應改變，可接受容忍提案被修正精進，有包容力採取適當措施或嘗試不同做法。

如果你喜歡HR而且不排斥豐富的工作，對選訓育用留等不同職能輪調有接受度，歡迎來與我們認識 !

日期：2015-05-18

本所修正語文能力證明檢定標準，104學年度前入學者依照原訂定標準。以下規定適用104學年度後入學之新生，不溯及既往。

 

(一) 英語：TOEFL成績以電腦計分者為iBT61以上（原計分方式500）；TOEIC（多益）考試成績應達605以上；全民英檢通過中高級測驗。

 

(二)修習第二外語應達下列標準：

 1.日語：日文檢測應通過第三級（N3）以上。

 2.德語：應通過德語A2檢定考試。

 3.法語：應通過法語A2檢定考試。

 

(三) 外籍生如將中文視為第二外國語者，修訂為應通過「華語文能力測驗」高等第5級。

 

 ◎ 英語檢定未達前項標準者，TOEIC（多益）英語檢定考試達三次，其中一次成績470分以上或修習英語兩百小時以上，視為通過語文能力之要求，其餘相關規定依照原訂定標準

 

 ◎本語文能力證明規定適用於104學年度後入學之新生（包括104當學年），不溯及既往。

 

1.95-1-1所務會議修正通過【95.10.12】;2.96-2-02所務會議修正通過【97.04.21】;3.98-2-1所務會議修正通過【99.03.08】;4.103-1-1所務會議通過【103.12.02】;5.103-2-2所務會議通過【104.05.12】

【103學年度新生學生證領取相關注意事項】

一、103學年度新生學生證自9月10日(星期三)起發放，請同學攜帶有照片之身分證明文件至行政大樓四樓教務處註冊組各學系(所)櫃台領取。

三、僑生(含港澳生)請洽學務處生僑組葉巧雯小姐領取，校內分機63011。

四、大陸地區學位生請洽學務處生僑組盧誼甄小姐領取，校內分機62227。

六、國際學生請洽國際合作事務處何芸婷小姐領取，校內分機62040。

七、依本校學則第十條及十三條規定：新生應依規定完成入學手續，若於103學年度第1學期延誤註冊逾二週仍未完成註冊繳費，將逕予註銷學籍。並通知悠遊卡公司註銷學生證悠遊卡功能，如卡片已有儲值，請持卡人逕行至臺北捷運各車站旅客詢問處申請退費事宜。
